admission.justification: Two readings of one flag were weighed, and the choice decides what a caller may conclude from a page that ends a seed.

alternatives.option: State enumeration completeness for the seed the page finished, and name the next seed in the continuation
alternatives.reason: A page can know that it reached the end of its own seed; it cannot know the total without enumerating everything, which the page bound forbids. The continuation carries the rest of the walk, so nothing is lost.

alternatives.option: State one completion flag for the whole walk
alternatives.reason: It would have to be false on every page until the last, and then a caller reading a finished seed could not tell whether that seed is done.
alternatives.reconsider_when: a caller needs a single walk-level completion fact, for example a bounded answer that must say how much of the tree it covered.

consequences: `enumerationComplete` describes a seed, and `continuation` names the next one; the two are read together.
Skill c-04 states the same reading, and a caller that ignores the continuation under-reports coverage rather than being misled about it.
context: A paged walk crosses several seeds. A page can finish the seed it was walking while other seeds remain, and the page has to say both facts without claiming knowledge of the whole walk.
decider: the developer, as the MIK-R73@v1 appendix row 59 states it
